content: We must indulge the mind and from time to time allow it the leisure which is its food and strength.
author: Seneca
sourceWork: De Tranquillitate Animi (On Tranquility of Mind)
story:
There is a sharp, grounded clarity in this observation. Thinking about doing something gives us a comfortable dopamine hit of progress without any of the actual friction. We often use over-researching and planning as socially acceptable disguises for fear of starting.

Seneca understood that real peace is never won by escaping the world or blaming external circumstances. Clarity follows action; it does not precede it. You cannot think your way into a new way of living—you have to act your way into a new way of understanding. The smallest real-world step beats the most brilliant theory.
reflectionPrompt: What would change in your daily outlook if you truly lived by this perspective?
